title: Where China's Great Wall Ends — Alone in the Desert · Silk Road EP6 | China Travel Expert
description:
Everyone photographs the Great Wall on its green mountains near Beijing. But follow it west and it simply runs out of mountains — and ends, alone, on the edge of the Gobi.

Its final fort is Jiayuguan, the westernmost pass of the Ming Great Wall in Gansu. It was begun in 1372 by the officer Feng Sheng — nine years before Shanhaiguan at the eastern end — and out here, away from the grey brick of the Beijing sections, the wall is built mainly of loess, desert earth tamped in solid layers. In 1873 the general Zuo Zongtang had it named "天下第一雄关" — the First and Greatest Pass Under Heaven. West of its gate: nothing but the Gobi, the road every Silk Road caravan had to take.

🧭 Expert Tip: Jiayuguan has its own high-speed-rail station (Jiayuguan South) — come at sunset, when the loess walls turn gold and the desert goes quiet.

长城的尽头，不在北京的青山，而在戈壁边上——天下第一雄关，嘉峪关。
